job.title: Head of Health Technology Partnerships
job.description:
• Lead commercial growth across a specialist health technology portfolio.
  • Build partnerships with healthcare providers, technology vendors and sector stakeholders.
  • Growth-focused role within a 100% Māori-owned telecommunications, broadcast and health technology group.

The opportunity
Tū Ātea Network Services is a 100% Māori-owned group operating across telecommunications, broadcasting, media, health technology and infrastructure services.

The organisation is seeking a commercially driven Head of Health Technology Partnerships to grow its health technology portfolio. This is not a clinical, operational or healthcare service delivery role. It is a market-facing commercial role focused on business development, customer growth, strategic partnerships and recurring revenue.

You will work with healthcare providers, aged care organisations, technology partners, suppliers and sector stakeholders to identify new opportunities, grow existing accounts and position Tū Ātea Network Services as a trusted provider of health technology products and services.

Healthcare sector credibility matters, but this role is for someone who can turn relationships into commercial growth.


About you
You may come from health technology, medical technology, digital health, clinical communications, health ICT, enterprise technology, managed services or another healthcare-adjacent commercial environment.

You will bring:
  • Business development, account management or commercial growth experience.
  • Experience selling or partnering across healthcare environments.
  • A track record of revenue growth, account expansion or new market development.
  • Confidence working with healthcare executives, procurement teams, technology partners and senior stakeholders.
  • Strong commercial, negotiation and relationship management capability.
  • The ability to understand customer needs and shape practical technology-led solutions.
This is a strong opportunity for a commercially minded health-sector operator who wants to build a growth portfolio within a Māori-owned technology and infrastructure group.

For a confidential discussion, please contact:
Richard Gray-Smith
Director, Executive Leadership and Search

job.title: General Manager, Partnerships
job.description:
• Lead commercial growth across teleco, broadcasting, media and health technology.
  • Shape market strategy, product proposition and recurring revenue growth.
  • Executive role with competitive remuneration and performance-based incentives.

The opportunity
Tū Ātea Network Services Limited is a 100% Māori-owned group at the forefront of telecommunications, broadcasting, media, health technology and infrastructure services across Aotearoa.

Through strategic acquisitions including Broadtech, JDA and Transworks, TANS brings together deep capability across nationwide transmission networks, broadcast and media environments, telecommunications infrastructure, healthcare and aged care technology, utilities, data centres, switching, routing, optical networks and industrial electrical systems.

Broadtech has been a trusted leader in New Zealand’s telecommunications and broadcast infrastructure for over 50 years, while JDA owns and operates broadcast and telecommunications transmission sites, including digital terrestrial television network infrastructure. Transworks brings specialist systems integration capability across core, switching, routing, optical and industrial electrical environments.

TANS is now seeking a General Manager, Partnerships to lead its market-facing commercial growth agenda.

This is not a passive partnerships role. It is an executive commercial role for someone with business development edge, entrepreneurial drive and the ability to turn market opportunity into sustained revenue growth.

You will lead a senior commercial team across sales, business development, market engagement and sector growth, working closely with the CEO and Executive Leadership Team to sharpen market focus, strengthen product proposition, deepen customer and supplier partnerships, and build more predictable revenue streams.


About you
You are likely to be a senior commercial, sales or business development leader from telecommunications, broadcasting, media technology, IT infrastructure, managed services, network services, health technology, industrial technology or another complex B2B technical environment.

You will bring:
  • Executive-level commercial, sales or business development leadership experience.
  • A clear track record of revenue growth and market expansion.
  • Strong product proposition, go-to-market and deal-structuring capability.
  • Credibility with senior customers, suppliers, Boards and executives.
  • Experience leading commercial or market-facing teams.
  • The ability to operate across complex technical markets and translate capability into customer value.
  • Pace, resilience, commercial instinct and disciplined execution.
This is a rare opportunity to shape commercial growth across a future-focused, Māori-owned organisation with national reach, strong technical capability and genuine growth headroom.

For someone who is at their best where strategy meets the market, and where opportunity needs to become revenue, this is worth a conversation.

job.title: Head of Marketing
job.description:
• Join the Senior Leadership Team, reporting directly to the CEO
  • Lead a large team through four experienced senior direct reports
  • Oversee brand, creative, production and visual merchandising

With 59 stores, national reach and more than a century of history, Farmers is a business recognised across generations. 

Farmers is seeking an accomplished Head of Marketing as part of the Senior Leadership Team.  

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, this is a broad and influential leadership appointment. The role brings together brand and retail marketing, creative, design and production, TV, Catalogue, social media, in-store activation and visual merchandising. 

Through four senior direct reports, you will lead a multidisciplinary team of 64 people. Farmers operates with considerable capability in-house, including its creative, photographic and production studios. The scale is substantial, as is the opportunity to bring clarity, consistency and commercial focus to how that capability is deployed. 

The role requires a leader who can connect brand ambition with the realities of a complex retail environment—aligning marketing with merchandise, stores, customer behaviour and commercial priorities. 

You will be an experienced marketing executive who has led a large marketing team within retail, FMCG or another significant consumer-facing organisation. You will understand both traditional and digital channels and know how to turn customer insight into relevant, effective activity. 

Just as importantly, you will bring mature judgement, a pragmatic leadership style and the ability to build trust across a longstanding and highly engaged business. 

This is a rare opportunity: stewardship of one of New Zealand’s most recognised brands, leadership of a significant marketing operation and the chance to influence the experience Farmers creates for its customers nationwide. 

If you have led a complex consumer marketing function and are drawn to the opportunity to work with an iconic New Zealand brand, apply now. 

As part of the James Pascoe Group, you’ll have access to a range of exclusive benefits, including generous discounts across the other James Pascoe Group companies, as well as special offers with Southern Cross Health Insurance, ANZ Banking and Specsavers. You’ll also have the opportunity to tap into the expertise, knowledge and experience of the other retail businesses, providing valuable opportunities to share ideas and learn from a diverse range of retail specialists.

job.title: Director Communications and Media
job.description:
• Shape how we communicate on matters affecting tamariki and rangatahi 
  • Deliver clear, consistent and impactful communications in a complex environment 
  • Drive media engagement, issues management and ministerial support

About Oranga Tamariki 
Oranga Tamariki works to ensure tamariki in Aotearoa are supported to flourish within loving whānau and communities. Guided by the belief that every child can thrive when surrounded by the right people and a safe, nurturing environment, more than 4,500 kaimahi work across the country to improve outcomes for tamariki, rangatahi and whānau. 

The Communications and Media function plays a critical role in helping the organisation tell its story, respond to scrutiny, engage effectively with stakeholders, and connect strategy with frontline delivery. This is an opportunity to lead that function at a pivotal time. 

 
About the Role 
This is one of the most senior communications roles in the New Zealand public sector. You'll shape strategy, media and stakeholder engagement for an agency operating at the centre of national scrutiny. Reporting to the Chief of Staff, you'll lead a team of around 26 across communications, media, content and channels – including web, social media, video and design - and be closely involved in the organisation’s most sensitive issues, including ministerial and government-facing communications. This is a hands on, close to the action role.  

This is a role that balances long term strategy with day-to-day responsiveness. One week you might be shaping an organisational communications strategy, strengthening internal engagement, or helping leaders think differently about connecting with frontline kaimahi. The next, you could be responding to urgent media issues, preparing material for ministerial engagement, or navigating sensitive public interest matters. 

Key areas of focus include: 
  • Leading the organisation's communications and media strategy 
  • Providing trusted advice to senior leaders and the Chief Executive 
  • Supporting ministerial and government facing communications 
  • Strengthening internal communications and employee engagement 
  • Driving digital communications and channels, including website, social media, content and design, to reach audiences more directly and creatively 
  • Building capability, accountability and consistency across the communications function 
  • Strengthening stakeholder engagement across government and community partners 
  • Ensuring communications activity supports organisational priorities and delivers measurable impact 
This is a highly visible role with significant influence across the organisation and regular engagement with ministers, government agencies, media and external stakeholders. 

 
About You 
You are an experienced communications leader who combines strategic judgment with genuine hands-on credibility. You understand the realities of operating in a high-profile environment and can move comfortably between executive advisory work, media engagement, crisis communications and organisational leadership. 

What you’ll bring: 
  • Significant senior communications and media leadership experience 
  • Strong understanding of machinery of government and ministerial environments 
  • Experience working in organisations operating under public scrutiny or significant stakeholder interest 
  • A track record leading high-performing communications teams 
  • Expertise across strategic communications, media management and reputation management 
  • Confidence leading digital communications and channels, with exposure to web, social media, content and design, having driven growth in direct audience engagement 
  • The ability to provide clear, pragmatic advice in complex situations 
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and executive presence 
  • Understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and experience engaging with diverse communities across Aotearoa 
Most importantly, you're someone who can combine leadership with delivery. You'll be comfortable setting direction, making decisions, supporting your team, and stepping into the detail when required. 


Why This Role? 
Opportunities to lead communications at this level are rare. This role offers the chance to shape the voice, reputation and engagement approach of one of New Zealand's most important public sector organisations. You'll work alongside experienced leaders, influence issues of national significance, and lead a capable team with the mandate to make a genuine impact. 

This is a Wellington-based position. 
 

How to Apply 
INSIDE Recruitment is managing this appointment. To apply, please include a CV and cover letter outlining your experience. For a confidential discussion, please contact Jeremy McLeod (jeremy@inside.co.nz). Applications close 12pm, Friday 25th September. 
  
Please note: You must be eligible to work in Aotearoa and able to pass a Ministry of Justice criminal history check.

job.title: Chief Information and Security Officer
job.description:
• Enterprise-wide technology infrastructure and security mandate
  • Large-scale, regulated and 24-hour operating environment
  • Direct influence with executive leadership and the Board

SkyCity Entertainment Group is appointing a Chief Information and Security Officer to lead the functions that protect, sustain and strengthen its enterprise technology infrastructure environment. 

The mandate spans cyber security, infrastructure and technology operations, site reliability, application support, data engineering and data governance across SkyCity’s gaming, hospitality, entertainment and corporate operations. 

Reporting to the Chief Customer and Digital Officer, the CISO will lead the Group’s security and enterprise technology infrastructure. Working alongside the Group Digital Officer, they will ensure SkyCity’s digital ambitions are supported by secure, reliable and efficient platforms and services. 

The opportunity is to bring greater integration and effectiveness across a broad enterprise function. This includes strengthening cyber and operational resilience, improving critical service performance, and supporting technology innovation with expedience. 

The CISO will provide clear assurance to executive leadership, the Board and the Audit and Risk Committee, and lead the organisation’s response to significant technology and security incidents. 

The brief calls for a grounded, assured leader who remains composed under pressure and acts decisively when required. Intellectually curious and externally connected, they will stay ahead of emerging technology infrastructure and security developments, continually looking for better ways to strengthen services, reduce risk and enable the business. They will build trust across technical and business teams, strengthen accountability and bring people with them through change. 

We are interested in established CIOs, CISOs and senior technology executives who bring: 
  • Leadership experience within a large-scale, complex and continuously operating technology environment. 
  • Depth in cyber security, enterprise risk and regulatory assurance. 
  • Substantial accountability for infrastructure, technology operations, service delivery and business-critical applications. 
  • Experience maintaining resilient 24-hour services and leading the response to major outages or cyber incidents. 
  • Strong commercial judgement across investment, vendors and operating models. 
  • Credibility with executives, Boards, regulators and senior business leaders. 
  • A record of building capable leadership teams and delivering sustained change in complex organisations. 
Experience in a regulated, multi-site, customer-facing organisation will be highly regarded. 

This is a rare opportunity to influence the technology infrastructure and security direction of one of New Zealand’s most distinctive organisations, and to lead a function central to its resilience, performance and future. 

All enquiries and applications will be treated in strict confidence.

job.title: Team Leader, National Standards Committee
job.description:
• Lead a high-performing team delivering meaningful public outcomes 
  • Navigate complex and high-profile complaints with confidence 
  • Influence the future of legal regulation in New Zealand

The New Zealand Law Society Te Kāhui Ture o Aotearoa plays a vital role in regulating New Zealand's legal profession and maintaining public confidence in legal services. Through the Lawyers Complaints Service, it manages complaints and professional conduct matters that are often complex, sensitive, and of significant public interest.  

 
About the Role 
Reporting to the Manager, National Standards & Investigations, you'll lead a highly capable team responsible for supporting National Standards Committees and managing some of the Lawyers Complaints Service's most challenging and high-profile matters.  

This is a unique opportunity for a people leader who thrives in complex environments. You'll provide strategic oversight of sensitive complaints, guide and develop an experienced team, identify and manage risk, and ensure matters progress effectively through the regulatory process.  

Alongside leading day-to-day operations, you'll have the opportunity to influence process improvements, support organisational change initiatives, and contribute to the ongoing evolution of the complaints service.  


What You'll Bring 
You're an experienced leader with the confidence to operate in a highly scrutinised environment, balancing strong people leadership with sound judgement and risk awareness.  


Ideally, you'll bring: 
  • Proven experience leading and developing high-performing teams 
  • Experience in complaints, investigations, regulatory, disciplinary, legal, ombudsman, or similar environments 
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills 
  • The ability to navigate complexity, ambiguity, and competing priorities 
  • Sound judgement, resilience, and a calm, pragmatic approach under pressure 
  • Experience interpreting legislation, policy, or regulatory frameworks is highly desirable.  

Why Join? 
This is a rare opportunity to lead a highly regarded team working on complex and meaningful matters that help maintain trust in New Zealand's legal profession. 

You'll join a collaborative, high-performing team and a supportive leadership environment that values autonomy, fresh thinking, and continuous improvement. Alongside intellectually stimulating work, you'll have the opportunity to influence the future of complaints management and make a lasting impact across the profession. 

 
Apply Now 
To submit your application, please click to Apply or for a confidential discussion, contact Fraser Leith at fraser@inside.co.nz. All applications will be acknowledged electronically.

job.title: Commercial Lead
job.description:
• Drive revenue growth, market engagement, and commercial performance 
  • Build influential relationships across a professional services environment 
  • Shape the future direction of a growing education and events portfolio 

About the role: 
Reporting into the Commercial Manager, we're seeking a commercially minded and relationship-focused Commercial Lead to drive the growth and performance of a portfolio of professional development programmes, events, and learning solutions. 

This is a newly established role created as part of an ambitious growth strategy. You'll identify market opportunities, build trusted industry relationships, and develop a strong pipeline of relevant, high-value offerings that support professionals to stay informed, connected, and ahead of emerging trends. 

Working at the intersection of commercial growth, stakeholder engagement, and product development, you'll use market intelligence, industry insight, and customer feedback to identify opportunities, attract leading subject matter experts, and bring new products and services to market. 

Success in this role will be measured through revenue growth, increased market engagement, stronger industry partnerships, and the development of commercially successful products that respond to evolving professional needs. 
 

Key responsibilities: 
  • Drive revenue growth and portfolio performance through the development of commercially successful products, services, and learning solutions. 
  • Build trusted relationships across the profession, engaging industry leaders, stakeholders, presenters, and subject matter experts to create valuable partnerships and opportunities. 
  • Stay ahead of market trends, identifying emerging issues, legislative developments, and customer needs to inform product development and commercial decision-making. 

What you'll bring: 
You are commercially astute, naturally curious, and thrive on building meaningful professional relationships. You enjoy identifying opportunities, influencing stakeholders, and turning ideas into successful commercial outcomes. 

 
You'll also bring: 
  • Experience in professional services, legal, consulting, recruitment, membership, education, financial services, or a similar relationship-led environment 
  • A proven track record in business development, partnership management, account management, or commercial growth 
  • Strong relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills 
  • The confidence and credibility to engage with senior professionals and subject matter experts 
  • Strong research, market awareness, and opportunity-spotting capability 
  • A proactive, self-directed approach and the ability to work autonomously 

What we offer: 
This is an exciting opportunity to join a purpose-led organisation at a time of growth and transformation. You'll have the opportunity to shape the role, build an influential professional network, and make a meaningful contribution to the future success of a highly respected organisation. 

We offer a collaborative and supportive culture, flexible hybrid working arrangements, and the chance to work alongside people committed to professional excellence and continuous learning. 

To submit your application, please click “Apply now”. For a confidential discussion, contact Fraser Leith at fraser@inside.co.nz. All applications will be acknowledged electronically.

job.title: Senior Risk Manager
job.description:
• Senior enterprise risk role with broad organisational visibility
  • Work with senior leaders on complex, business-critical risks
  • Auckland preferred, other New Zealand locations considered

This is a senior enterprise risk role for someone who wants their work to be close to real business decisions.

You’ll be joining a large, complex New Zealand organisation with an established approach to risk management already in place. The foundations are strong, the work is visible, and the opportunity is to bring fresh thinking, sound judgement and practical challenge to an environment that is ready for the next layer of maturity.

This is not a role for someone who wants to simply maintain a risk register. It will suit someone who enjoys working with senior people, asking good questions, making sense of ambiguity, and turning complex issues into clear, useful insight.


About the role
As Senior Manager Risk, you will work across the organisation to support effective enterprise risk management.

You will partner with senior leaders to help identify, assess, monitor and report key risks. You will contribute to senior management and governance-level reporting, support the ongoing improvement of risk frameworks and processes, and help leaders make better-informed decisions.

The role works across a broad range of risk areas. These may include commercial, operational, regulatory, supplier, technology, project, financial, reputational and resilience-related risks.

You will not personally own every risk across the organisation. Your role is to help ensure the right risks are visible, well understood, appropriately owned, actively managed and clearly reported.

This is an influential role in a matrix environment, where outcomes are delivered through others. Success will come through credibility, relationships, judgement and the ability to bring people with you.


What success looks like
After 12 months, you will be known as someone who has lifted the quality of risk conversations across the organisation.

You will have built trust with senior leaders, improved the clarity of risk reporting, and helped connect risks that may otherwise have sat in separate parts of the business.

You will have brought useful challenge to an established risk environment, without trying to change things for the sake of it.

You will have helped make enterprise risk more practical, more visible and more useful to decision-making.

That is the heart of this role: making sure risk is not just reported, but understood.


What you’ll be doing
  • Providing practical enterprise risk advice to senior leaders
  • Supporting senior management and governance-level risk reporting
  • Helping identify, assess and monitor key and emerging risks
  • Supporting the use of risk appetite and tolerance in decision-making
  • Maintaining and improving risk frameworks, policies and processes
  • Working across multiple business functions to build a joined-up view of risk
  • Helping lift risk capability through guidance, facilitation and coaching
  • Bringing constructive challenge and fresh thinking to an established risk environment

About you
You will be an experienced enterprise risk professional who can operate credibly with senior stakeholders while staying practical and grounded.

You may currently be in a role such as Senior Risk Manager, Enterprise Risk Manager, Risk Governance Manager, Principal Risk Advisor, Risk and Compliance Manager, Head of Risk and Assurance, or a comparable senior risk role.

You will bring:
  • Strong experience in enterprise risk, risk governance or risk and compliance
  • Experience working in a large, complex or highly governed organisation
  • A practical understanding of enterprise risk frameworks
  • Experience contributing to senior management, executive or governance-level reporting
  • Exposure to risk appetite, risk tolerance, key risk and emerging risk processes
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills
  • The ability to simplify complex issues and communicate clearly
  • Sound judgement, curiosity and commercial awareness
  • Confidence to challenge constructively
  • A continuous improvement mindset
Experience from large corporate, infrastructure, utilities, telecommunications, financial services, insurance, banking, government, Crown entity, listed company or other complex environments would be relevant.

The right person will be thoughtful, credible and commercially aware. You will be comfortable working with ambiguity, confident enough to challenge, and pragmatic enough to bring people with you.

This role will suit someone who wants enterprise risk to be useful, visible and connected to real business decisions.


Location
Auckland is preferred, although candidates from other New Zealand locations may be considered where there is strong alignment to the role.


How to apply
Please apply online with your CV.

Suitable candidates will be contacted and provided with further information about the organisation, role and process.

  • Maintaining and improving risk frameworks, policies and processes
  • Working across multiple business functions to build a joined-up view of risk
  • Helping lift risk capability through guidance, facilitation and coaching
  • Bringing constructive challenge and fresh thinking to an established risk environment

About you
You will be an experienced enterprise risk professional who can operate credibly with senior stakeholders while staying practical and grounded.

You may currently be in a role such as Senior Risk Manager, Enterprise Risk Manager, Risk Governance Manager, Principal Risk Advisor, Risk and Compliance Manager, Head of Risk and Assurance, or a comparable senior risk role.

You will bring:
  • Strong experience in enterprise risk, risk governance or risk and compliance
  • Experience working in a large, complex or highly governed organisation
  • A practical understanding of enterprise risk frameworks
  • Experience contributing to senior management, executive or governance-level reporting
  • Exposure to risk appetite, risk tolerance, key risk and emerging risk processes
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills
  • The ability to simplify complex issues and communicate clearly
  • Sound judgement, curiosity and commercial awareness
  • Confidence to challenge constructively
  • A continuous improvement mindset
Experience from large corporate, infrastructure, utilities, telecommunications, financial services, insurance, banking, government, Crown entity, listed company or other complex environments would be relevant.

The right person will be thoughtful, credible and commercially aware. You will be comfortable working with ambiguity, confident enough to challenge, and pragmatic enough to bring people with you.

This role will suit someone who wants enterprise risk to be useful, visible and connected to real business decisions.


Location
Auckland is preferred, although candidates from other New Zealand locations may be considered where there is strong alignment to the role.


How to apply
Please apply online with your CV.

Suitable candidates will be contacted and provided with further information about the organisation, role and process.

job.title: Legal and Commercial Advisor
job.description:
• Direct exposure to high impact investment decisions
  • Blend of legal, commercial and governance work 
  • Visible role in a newly established Crown Entity 

Join Invest New Zealand at an exciting moment in our journey. We’re a recently established Autonomous Crown Entity with a high-performance, collaborative culture — and we’re looking for a curious, practical legal professional who enjoys working at the intersection of investment, governance, and great process.


About us
Our purpose is to increase the flow of foreign direct investment into sectors with high growth and productivity potential — supporting long-term economic prosperity. We work on investments typically in the $100m to $1b range and help deliver the investment component of the Active Investor Plus (AIP) Visa scheme.


The opportunity
As our Legal & Commercial Advisor, you’ll play a key role in how we assess and support acceptable investments under the AIP visa programme. You’ll lead the investment product assessment work and support the AIP decision makers — making sure they have clear, timely information and that decisions and records are managed in line with relevant legal and regulatory requirements.


What you’ll be doing
  • Be the go-to person for queries about AIP investment criteria and process, working closely with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Pre-assess managed fund and direct investment applications and prepare clear summaries and recommendations for decision makers.
  • Maintain accurate records, including processes/procedures and material correspondence with applicants.
  • Own key risk management processes for the programme, including re-certification and the risk log.
  • Support relationships with key stakeholders such as Government agencies, fund managers and licensed immigration advisers.
  • Assist the General Counsel with Official Information Act requests from time to time.
 
What you’ll bring
  • An admitted lawyer (commerce and/or finance qualifications are an advantage).
  • 4–6 years’ PQE, including at least 2 years in private practice.
  • Strong commercial judgement and a sound understanding of the managed funds environment (or the motivation to learn quickly, supported by commercial/financial services experience).
  • Confidence working with governance and reporting requirements; board secretariat or legal executive experience is a bonus.
  • Understanding of New Zealand’s financial services regulatory environment.
  • A detail-focused mindset with the ability to assess and appropriately challenge information.
  • Clear, professional communication skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.
  • A naturally curious, collaborative style—you enjoy being part of a small team and pitching in where needed.

Why join us?
You’ll be joining a small, ambitious organisation where your work will be visible and valued. We’re building strong foundations and practical ways of working—so you’ll have genuine scope to improve process, influence how we operate, and work alongside experienced colleagues who care about doing great work (and doing it well together).
